Hey Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the batching/cache stuff you showed; for our use case (high-fanout customer support classification) latency matters but token costs are the bigger driver.

Before we sign an NDA, can you sketch how pilot pricing typically works for Optimize (credits/commit tiers, how cache credits get consumed, and whether quantized model variants are eligible for the same discounts)? We have a procurement review next Thursday and want to present a concrete pilot ask.

Quick details about ClearStream: expected pilot volume ~1.5M tokens/week, peak P95 latency requirement ~200ms, and we want to exercise both prefix caching and a pre-warm KV cache for repeated prompts.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Claire Nguyen
Head of Platform, ClearStream Labs
claire@clearstream.ai

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Quick question on Optimize toolkit for a pilot

Claire —

Appreciate the notes and the traffic details. Below is a compact pilot sketch tailored for a cache-first setup + quantization pathing. This is a commercial sketch (not a final SOW) but should give procurement what they need for next week.

High-level pilot structure
- Duration: 8 weeks (proof-of-value)
- Committed credits: 12M token-credits (prepaid) — covers baseline consumption at expected volume plus a 20% buffer
- Discounting: standard pilot discount 25% off hosted list for Optimize features; we can consider an incremental concession up to 15% off the pilot rate for contract signatures within 14 days of pilot start (requires manager approval)

How credits & cache interact (key points)
- Cache-first billing model: cached token hits consume a lightweight "cache-token" unit (roughly 10% of full token cost) while misses consume normal token credits.
- Prefix caching: works with the hosted model variants we provide — cached prefixes are eligible for cache-token pricing.
- KV cache pre-warm: pre-warm requests count as normal tokens during the pre-warm window; subsequent hits are charged at cache-token rate.
- Reporting: Console shows token-level breakdown by cache hit/miss and per-route cost. We'll add a pilot dashboard link for ClearStream.

Quantization & model variants
- Supported quantized variants: int8 and int4 trimmed variants we host.
- Recommendation: start pilot on int8 variant for parity testing (same-quality baseline) and enable int4 for fast-path experiments.
- Discount implications: quantized variants are eligible for the same pilot discount, but we treat int4 as a "fast-path" variant with discretionary rate adjustments if usage skews >60% to int4 at scale.

Ops & SLAs
- Latency: our Dedicated pools will aim to meet P95 200ms for the pilot if you enable the "priority" queue (small monthly premium applies).
- Fallbacks: auto-fallback to the next compatible variant if capacity constrained — billed at the variant rate.

Attachments: I attached a short MAP (pilot-MAP-20270505.pdf) and a one-page quant rulesheet (optimize-quant-rulesheet.xlsx) for your procurement team.

If this looks directionally right, I can propose a 1-hour walk-through next Tue or Wed to align on telemetry and success criteria.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Jonas —

Thanks, this is super helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement & infra:
1) For the cache-token unit (10% estimate) — can you commit to a maximum bound (e.g., no more than 15% of full token pricing) for the pilot so we can model worst-case spend?
2) If we move to int4 aggressively during the pilot and it causes regressions in quality, will Redwood help with rollbacks/auto-fallback policies at no extra ops cost?
3) Do you provide a burn-rate alert that triggers when us hitting 75% of committed credits? Ideally HubSpot or Slack integration.

Procurement also asked for an example SOW line item for finance: — "Pilot credits: 12,000,000 token-credits prepaid at net $X after discount; additional consumption billed at list rate." Can you provide the net per-token price we should put in the SOW example (ballpark is fine).

Claire
